transcript:
Agent: Thank you for calling Cardholder Services. My name is Marcus. How can I help you today?
Customer: Hi Marcus. I'm calling because I have a charge on my card from Skyward Air, but I never got my flight.
Agent: I can certainly look into that for you. May I please have your full name and your billing zip code to pull up your account?
Customer: Yes, my name is Grace Mbeki, and the zip code is 30312.
Agent: Thank you, Ms. Mbeki. I have your profile open now. Could you share the date of the charge and the exact amount?
Customer: It was on August 22nd, and the amount was $388.40.
Agent: I see that transaction right here from Skyward Air for $388.40 on August 22nd. Could you tell me a little more about what happened with the booking?
Customer: The airline cancelled the flight on their end. They told me I would get a refund back to my card, but that was six weeks ago and I haven't seen anything.
Agent: Did they send you any documentation or an email regarding the flight being cancelled and the return of your payment?
Customer: Yes, they sent an email when they called off the flight saying the money would be sent back to my original payment method in a couple of weeks.
Agent: Okay. Did you accept any flight credits, vouchers, or rebooking options from them?
Customer: No, nothing like that. They said it would be sent straight back to the card.
Agent: Have you had any additional communication with Skyward Air since that initial message?
Customer: I tried calling their customer line about a week ago, but I was on hold forever and couldn't get through to a real person.
Agent: Thank you for those details. Just to ensure I have recorded everything accurately, you were charged $388.40 by Skyward Air on August 22nd, the airline cancelled the flight and promised a return to your card six weeks ago, and you have not received the funds or accepted any alternative travel credit.
